criteria_verification.notes: KeycloakIdentityProvider implements 3-member IdentityProvider port with sync currentPrincipal backed by _currentPrincipal field. Test suite (15/15 passed) validates implementation.
Silent-then-interactive sign-in flow implemented. Tests verify silent refresh precedes interactive PKCE S256 browser flow.
Interactive flow uses KeycloakConfig.redirectUrl and requests offline_access. Tests validate configuration parameters.
Distinct SignInCancelled and SignInFailed exceptions surface cancel vs failure outcomes. Test suite validates distinction.
Single-flight guard using _signInInFlight Future tracking. Tests verify concurrent calls result in single flow.
Proactive refresh scheduled 5 minutes before access-token expiry. Tests verify refresh occurs and principal remains available.
Generation-based race protection ensures signOut() wins over in-flight refresh. Tests verify sign-out during refresh leaves currentPrincipal null.
Background refresh try-catch clears _currentPrincipal on failure. Tests verify graceful degradation to signed-out state.
Constructor initializes _currentPrincipal to null. Tests verify absent/unreadable sessions treated as signed out.
FakeAppAuth and FakeSecureSessionStore provide hermetic test isolation. All 15 tests use fakes with no external dependencies.

Runtime parity check (flutter analyze) found 2 unused_catch_stack warnings at test/adapters/keycloak_identity_provider_test.dart:58:19 and 78:19. AC-011 requires zero errors. Player claimed 'zero errors' but deterministic verification contradicts this.

rationale: AC-001 through AC-010 are verified with excellent test coverage (93.99%) and 15/15 hermetic tests passing. However, AC-011 is definitively violated: the orchestrator's independent flutter analyze run found 2 unused_catch_stack warnings in the task's test file. The Player claimed AC-011 was complete with zero errors, but the runtime_parity check provides deterministic proof otherwise. This is a simple fix: remove unused stack parameters from two catch blocks.
